_readme: Content rules for build_resources_page.py, per spec SITE-06 D4 and its findings 13 and 14.
These are refusals and not warnings, because the register's input is prose typed by
colleagues who were never told the rules. A warning printed at 4pm is a warning nobody reads.
Extend a list here rather than in the generator, and say in the commit why the entry was added.

_why: The track's routing mapping is canonical, not a tone preference. A public list of what
to read next is the track routing people, so a programme that is not a default route
must not arrive on it by a contributor's good intentions.
Match is case-insensitive and on whole words, so an author affiliated with one of these
institutions can still be cited by name without tripping the rule; only the programme
being named as a route trips it.
Recorded here so a later session can see what the rule sends people TO, not only what
it keeps off. Not enforced; there is no sensible refusal for failing to mention these.
The site's no-partner-org-in-sensitive-context rule. At least six of the seventeen Bali
participants are India-based, which is the context the rule exists for: a public page
that pairs a named sending organization with named local work is a disclosure about
people who did not choose it.
A resource's PUBLISHER is not a partner org, which is why this list names sending and
The track states its own pathway positively and never by contrast with another one.
A comparison reads as a claim about the other pathway's quality, which is not this
page's to make and is not what a reading list is for.
